lots.what_it_is: Pictorial painted bark cloth (tapa, called siapo or ngatu) from Wallis (Uvea), Wallis and Futuna, about 53 x 200 cm, in two scenes: a village scene (house, seated women with shell necklaces, a standing woman, pineapple, palms, flowers) and a sea scene (outrigger sailing canoe with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail, lobster, crab, octopus, fish, ray), with wavy red-brown and black and white geometric borders and black cloth hanging sleeves at both ends. Mua is a district of Wallis, so the title's 'by Mua Wallis' misreads a place name as a maker.
lots.score_reason: Credible identification as a rare pictorial Wallis type (Te Papa holds a near twin attributed to the 1960s), but the realistic Australian auction value is modest: generic tapa made A$10 to A$320 in the last 24 months, an early pictorial Tongan cloth passed at A$500, and a near-identical Wallis land-sea runner passed at EUR 80 in 2010. The upside is in a specialist Pacific sale (Webb's sold a smaller pictorial Uvea piece for NZD 950 in 2023). Scored for roughly A$150 to A$400, discounted for unverified age and the optimistic dealer ask.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of photo 3 reads 'Mua Wallis' on the canoe sail (a place inscription, not a signature). The composition matches Te Papa FE012568 (record opened, https://collections.tepapa.govt.nz/object/1086286: Wallis and Futuna, attributed to the 1960s, 762 x 1985 mm, 'a rare example of tapa decorated with pictorial references', the same canoe with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail and a village scene, bought from a French brocante in 2010, no price) and the 1stdibs dealer piece (same two-scene layout, island name on the canoe). It also resembles a narrow 'terre-mer' Wallis runner (43 x 165 cm) that passed at EUR 80 in Marseille in 2010, which suggests a repeated decorative or trade type rather than a one-off. Black sleeves are stitched to both ends for hanging; the dark red-brown pigment is glossy (a traditional glossy dye or a later coating, not determinable from the photos).
lots.condition: Looks intact in the photos, with no holes or tears visible; creases, folds and wavy uneven edges; glossy finish on the dark pigment; hanging sleeves stitched on. The back is not shown, so staining, insect damage, brittleness or repairs cannot be judged. Age unverified.

Australian auction results in the last 24 months are A$300 to A$1,250 hammer (median about A$440), so a real value of roughly A$300 to A$600 at a local auction. lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of photo 2: oval gold Singer medallion with a clearly legible 222K cartouche beneath it; SINGER decal on the arm; a small gold stamp left of the badge ending 'BRITAIN' (Made in Great Britain, partly legible); the base is in two parts with a seam under the bed, which is the 222K free-arm bed extension. Serial number not visible. Photo 1: tall black case with the foot controller clipped in the lid, a tan box (looks empty), a box of presser feet and attachments, a white box holding two metal embroidery hoop rings, and a red tray. Photo 3: modern black flex with a moulded Australian 3-pin plug (not original), red tray of thread and notions, and a folded or rolled paper item at the side (possibly the instruction booklet, not legible).
lots.condition: Machine glossy with decals largely intact and light wear to the bed and base; case scuffed with a worn lining; power lead replaced with a modern one, so an electrical safety check is advisable; Armitage says going order but I could not see it run; serial, bobbin case and bed extension latch unchecked.

lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos checked with enlarged crops. One-piece oval top with a moulded edge in a straight-grained reddish timber, refinished with a patchy orange-brown polish, small dark spots, and a short break or join in the edge moulding at the front (photo 3). The frieze is a much paler honey-coloured figured timber with a visible vertical joint, unlike the top and base, so it may be a different or replacement timber, or the top has been stained darker. Ring-turned and gadrooned baluster column with a dark collar; four leaf-carved, scroll-shouldered cabriole legs ending in scroll toes; white ceramic castors on all four legs. No underside, tilt catch, label or stamp shown. At 117 x 87 cm it is smaller than most comparables (134 to 154 cm long).
lots.condition: Base looks sound and complete, carving crisp, all four castors present. Top refinished, patchy and faded, with small dark marks and a split or join in the front edge moulding. Frieze timber does not match the top or base. Tilt mechanism, column joint and underside not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does the top tilt and does the catch work, and is the column firm with no wobble or repaired legs? What timber is the top, solid or veneered, and is the pale frieze original or a replacement (if the table is Australian cedar, blackwood or Huon pine rather than English mahogany it would interest local buyers more)? Is the mark at the front edge a crack or an old join? Are all four ceramic castors original and turning?

lots.guide_summary: Mostly SOLD. Close whole-lot comparables (tubs or boxes of built modern LEGO) sold for $55 to $130 hammer in Tasmania between Feb and Oct 2026: Armitage $80 and $105 (8 Jul 2026), Gowans $55 to $130 (7 lots). Same-item component sales (US eBay via PriceCharting, built or loose, no box): Dobby A$7.19 to A$28.74 (typical A$14), Mandrake A$24.66 to A$50.28 (typical A$29), Aragog A$4.67 to A$10.42, and the three orphan Speed Champions booklets A$10.06 to A$14.37 each; the identified parts add up to about A$75 at the lowest and A$91 at typical prices, before fees and postage. Category guides (other Armitage and Gowans LEGO lots, two boxed sets, bulk tubs, train lots) ran $35 to $150 hammer. No UNSOLD result found. Hammer prices exclude buyer's premium (Armitage 22%; Gowans premium extra). USD at 1.437 (ECB via frankfurter.dev, 16 Oct 2026).

lots.guide_summary: All AUD hammer, no conversion (rate 1.00). 8 close SOLD: Armitage's own room $25, $80 and $125 (Jul to Sep 2026) and Gowans $35 to $130 (Feb to Aug 2026). The three with about the same Carlton content as lot 563 (5 to 7 floral leaf pieces) made $35 (Gowans 416349), $50 (Gowans 408739) and $80 (Armitage lot 452, which also had uranium glass and decanters); larger all-Carlton groups made $90 to $130. Category guides, all SOLD: mixed china with a Carlton share $3 to $90; generic two-box china lots $25 to $100. Four Gowans lots naming Carlton passed in (420091 and its re-offer 421718, 422742 and its re-offer 424364) with no bid amount shown, so they are noted but not listed. No ASKING evidence found.
lots.working: Same-item set = lots with about the same Carlton content as lot 563 (5 to 7 floral leaf pieces) sold in the last 24 months: $35 (Gowans 416349, 19 Jun 2026), $50 (Gowans 408739, 15 May 2026) and $80 (Armitage lot 452, 9 Sep 2026). Keep: lowest $35 / 1.22 = $28.69, rounded down to $25 hammer ($30.50 all-in). Inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). The filler porcelain adds little. A flip has almost no margin, so this is a small keep buy only.
